enriched_entities.name: neurofibromin 1
enriched_entities.function: Tumor suppressor; GTPase activating protein (GAP) that negatively regulates RAS signaling pathway
biological_process: RAS protein signal transduction negative regulation
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Primary disease gene; NF1 haploinsufficiency impairs DNA repair and increases cancer susceptibility
enriched_entities.disease_relevance: Mutations cause Neurofibromatosis Type 1, characterized by neurofibromas, cafe-au-lait spots, and increased cancer risk

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II beta
enriched_entities.function: Controls DNA topology during transcription; resolves DNA tangles and supercoils by creating transient double-strand breaks
biological_process: DNA double-strand break formation and repair
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Primary mediator of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity; forms stable DNA-TOP2B-doxorubicin cleavage complexes in cardiomyocytes leading to persistent DNA damage
enriched_entities.cellular_location: Nucleus; constitutively expressed in non-dividing cardiomyocytes

enriched_entities.name: carbonyl reductase 1
enriched_entities.function: NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase; catalyzes two-electron reduction of carbonyl compounds including anthracyclines
biological_process: Anthracycline reduction to secondary alcohol metabolites
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Converts doxorubicin to doxorubicinol (C-13 hydroxyl metabolite) which accumulates in cardiac tissue and contributes to cardiotoxicity; polymorphisms (CBR1 V244M) associated with variable cardiotoxicity risk

enriched_entities.name: carbonyl reductase 3
enriched_entities.function: NADPH-dependent carbonyl reductase with substrate specificity overlapping CBR1; involved in xenobiotic metabolism
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Secondary carbonyl reductase contributing to doxorubicin metabolism and cardiotoxic metabolite formation; CBR3 polymorphisms may modulate individual cardiotoxicity susceptibility
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from literature and gene family homology (HGNC:1551 query returned incorrect gene; corrected via manual mapping)
enriched_entities.note: HGNC API returned CBX1 instead of CBR3; cross-references manually inferred from standard databases

enriched_entities.name: DNA topoisomerase II alpha
enriched_entities.function: Controls DNA topology during replication and mitosis; essential for chromosome segregation in dividing cells
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Primary therapeutic target of doxorubicin in cancer cells; doxorubicin stabilizes TOP2A-DNA cleavage complexes, leading to DNA damage and apoptosis in rapidly dividing tumor cells; overexpression or mutations associated with drug resistance
enriched_entities.cellular_location: Nucleus; highly expressed in proliferating cells

enriched_entities.name: ATP binding cassette subfamily B member 1
enriched_entities.function: ATP-dependent efflux pump that exports xenobiotics and therapeutic drugs from cells; major multidrug resistance protein
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Major mechanism of doxorubicin resistance; ABCB1 overexpression in tumor cells reduces intracellular doxorubicin concentration, limiting therapeutic efficacy; SNPs (C3435T, G2677T/A, C1236T) associated with altered drug disposition and toxicity
enriched_entities.cellular_location: Plasma membrane; apical surface of polarized cells

enriched_entities.name: tumor protein p53
enriched_entities.function: Master tumor suppressor and transcription factor; integrates stress signals to regulate cell cycle arrest, apoptosis, senescence, and DNA repair
biological_process: Transcriptional regulation of stress response genes
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Central to doxorubicin-induced apoptosis in both tumor and cardiac cells; p53 status determines treatment response - wild-type p53 promotes apoptosis following doxorubicin-induced DNA damage, while p53 mutations confer resistance and alter cardiotoxicity susceptibility
enriched_entities.disease_relevance: Most frequently mutated gene in human cancer; germline mutations cause Li-Fraumeni syndrome

enriched_entities.name: ralA binding protein 1
enriched_entities.function: Multifunctional protein involved in receptor-mediated endocytosis and glutathione-conjugate/xenobiotic transport; RalA effector protein
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Contributes to doxorubicin efflux and cellular resistance; transports glutathione-conjugated metabolites; RALBP1 depletion enhances chemosensitivity
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from phase1_anchor.json and standard gene databases

enriched_entities.name: superoxide dismutase 2
enriched_entities.function: Manganese-dependent mitochondrial enzyme that catalyzes dismutation of superoxide radicals to hydrogen peroxide and oxygen; primary mitochondrial antioxidant defense
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Critical for protecting cardiomyocytes from doxorubicin-induced mitochondrial oxidative stress; SOD2 polymorphisms (Ala16Val, rs4880) and expression levels modulate cardiotoxicity susceptibility; doxorubicin generates superoxide via redox cycling
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from phase1_anchor.json and standard gene databases

enriched_entities.name: glutathione S-transferase pi 1
enriched_entities.function: Phase II detoxification enzyme that catalyzes conjugation of glutathione to electrophilic compounds and reactive oxygen species
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Detoxifies doxorubicin-induced reactive oxygen species and electrophilic metabolites; GSTP1 polymorphisms (Ile105Val, rs1695) associated with variable cardiotoxicity and treatment response
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from phase1_anchor.json and standard gene databases

enriched_entities.name: glutathione S-transferase mu 1
enriched_entities.function: Phase II detoxification enzyme; conjugates glutathione to xenobiotics and reactive metabolites
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Detoxifies doxorubicin-induced reactive species; GSTM1-null genotype (homozygous deletion) present in 40-60% of populations, associated with increased susceptibility to oxidative stress and variable doxorubicin toxicity
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from phase1_anchor.json and standard gene databases

enriched_entities.name: solute carrier family 22 member 16
enriched_entities.function: Organic cation transporter facilitating cellular uptake of cationic compounds including doxorubicin
enriched_entities.role_in_context: Mediates doxorubicin uptake into cardiomyocytes; SLC22A16 expression levels and polymorphisms may influence cardiac drug accumulation and cardiotoxicity susceptibility; potential therapeutic target to reduce cardiac exposure
enriched_entities.provenance: Inferred from phase1_anchor.json and standard gene databases

enriched_entities.name: Doxorubicin
mechanism_of_action: Intercalates into DNA and stabilizes TOP2A-DNA cleavage complexes in cancer cells, causing DNA double-strand breaks and apoptosis
Generates reactive oxygen species through redox cycling, inducing oxidative stress
primary_targets: TOP2A (DNA topoisomerase II alpha) - therapeutic target in dividing cancer cells
TOP2B (DNA topoisomerase II beta) - cardiotoxicity mediator in cardiomyocytes
enriched_entities.major_toxicity: Cumulative dose-dependent cardiotoxicity leading to cardiomyopathy and congestive heart failure
enriched_entities.metabolism: Hepatic reduction by carbonyl reductases (CBR1, CBR3) to cardiotoxic metabolite doxorubicinol
enriched_entities.provenance: Standard pharmacology databases (ChEMBL API call failed due to CURIE format error; data inferred from phase1_anchor.json and DrugBank)

enriched_entities.name: Neurofibromatosis Type 1
enriched_entities.genetic_basis: Autosomal dominant disorder caused by loss-of-function mutations in NF1 gene (HGNC:7765) on chromosome 17q11.2
enriched_entities.mechanism_details: Haploinsufficiency or complete loss of neurofibromin (NF1 gene product) leads to constitutive RAS-MAPK pathway activation, impaired tumor suppression, and defective DNA repair
affected_pathways: RAS-MAPK signaling (hyperactivation due to loss of GAP activity)
cancer_predisposition: Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST) - 8-13% lifetime risk
enriched_entities.relevance_to_doxorubicin: NF1 patients with cancer may receive doxorubicin chemotherapy; underlying DNA repair deficiency may alter both therapeutic response and toxicity profiles; RAS pathway dysregulation may interact with doxorubicin-induced stress responses
enriched_entities.provenance: HGNC gene data, OMIM, and standard disease ontologies

evidence: NF1 encodes neurofibromin, a RAS-GTPase activating protein (GAP) that negatively regulates RAS signaling (hgnc_get_gene HGNC:7765)
NF1 disease is caused by heterozygous or homozygous loss-of-function mutations leading to constitutive RAS pathway activation (OMIM 162200)
Neurofibromin haploinsufficiency impairs tumor suppression and DNA repair capacity, increasing cancer susceptibility (standard NF1 disease literature)
NF1 is classified as a tumor suppressor gene; disease phenotype results from LOSS of normal protein function, not gain of aberrant function
Clinical features (neurofibromas, increased cancer risk) result from uncontrolled cell proliferation due to loss of RAS negative regulation
